before_F2: [F2] The Casimir element $\Omega=\sum_{ij}E_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}$ is independent of dual bases and central in $U(\mathfrak g)$, so its action on any module is a $\mathfrak g$-intertwiner; module actions extend uniquely to $U(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]], [[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]], [[lem-the-casimir-element-is-independent-of-dual-bases]], [[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]]).
after_F2: [F2] The Casimir tensor $\Omega=\sum_{ij}E_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}\in U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g)$ is independent of dual bases and invariant under the diagonal adjoint action: $[X\otimes1+1\otimes X,\Omega]=0$ for every $X\in\mathfrak g$. Indeed, for $X=E_{ab}$ the matrix-unit relations give the cancelling sum $\sum_jE_{aj}\otimes E_{jb}-\sum_iE_{ib}\otimes E_{ai}+\sum_iE_{ib}\otimes E_{ai}-\sum_jE_{aj}\otimes E_{jb}=0$, and linearity gives every $X$. Therefore its action on a tensor product of $\mathfrak g$-modules is a $\mathfrak g$-intertwiner. Module actions extend uniquely to $U(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]], [[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]], [[lem-the-casimir-element-is-independent-of-dual-bases]], [[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]]).
